preamble.summary: Proverbs 13 continues the antithetic-Solomonic-proverbs. Verse 24 — 'whoever spares the rod hates his son' — is the canonical-text-behind the 'spare the rod, spoil the child' proverbial saying (which Samuel Butler coined in Hudibras, 1664, paraphrasing this verse).
preamble.notable_variants: 13:7 'one pretends to be rich, yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth' — the inversion-of-appearances; 13:12 'hope deferred makes the heart sick'; 13:24 'spare the rod' proverbial basis.

variant_notes: 'A wise son hears his father's instruction, but a scoffer does not listen to rebuke' tracks MT.
'From the fruit of his mouth a man eats what is good, but the desire of the treacherous is for violence' tracks MT.

'Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life; he who opens wide his lips comes to ruin' tracks MT. GUARD-YOUR-MOUTH. James 3:2 ('if anyone does not stumble in what he says, he is a perfect man') extends.
'The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing, while the soul of the diligent is richly supplied' tracks MT.
'The righteous hates falsehood, but the wicked brings shame and disgrace' tracks MT.
'Righteousness guards him whose way is blameless, but sin overthrows the wicked' tracks MT.

'One pretends to be rich, yet has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth' tracks MT. APPEARANCE-INVERSION — 2 Cor 6:10 ('as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything') directly Christologically-extends.
'The ransom of a man's life is his wealth, but a poor man hears no threat' tracks MT.
'The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be put out' tracks MT.
'By insolence comes nothing but strife, but with those who take advice is wisdom' tracks MT.
'Wealth gained hastily will dwindle, but whoever gathers little by little will increase it' tracks MT.

'Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but a desire fulfilled is a tree of life' tracks MT. HOPE-DEFERRED-HEART-SICK. The DESIRE-FULFILLED-TREE-OF-LIFE — second wisdom-tree-of-life reference (cf. Prov 3:18).
'Whoever despises the word brings destruction on himself, but he who reveres the commandment will be rewarded' tracks MT.
'The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, that one may turn away from the snares of death' tracks MT. FOUNTAIN-OF-LIFE teaching (// Prov 10:11).
'Good sense wins favor, but the way of the treacherous is their ruin' tracks MT.
'Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool flaunts his folly' tracks MT.
'A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing' tracks MT.
'Poverty and disgrace come to him who ignores instruction, but whoever heeds reproof is honored' tracks MT.
'A desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but to turn away from evil is an abomination to fools' tracks MT.

'Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will suffer harm' tracks MT. WALK-WITH-WISE. 1 Corinthians 15:33 ('bad company corrupts good morals,' citing Menander) reflects the same ethic.
'Disaster pursues sinners, but the righteous are rewarded with good' tracks MT.

'A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, but the sinner's wealth is laid up for the righteous' tracks MT. WEALTH-OF-SINNER-TO-RIGHTEOUS — the eschatological-transfer. Ecclesiastes 2:26 echoes.
'The fallow ground of the poor would yield much food, but it is swept away through injustice' tracks MT.

'Whoever spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him is diligent to discipline him' tracks MT. SPARE-THE-ROD proverbial-source. The 'spare the rod, spoil the child' proverb was coined by Samuel Butler (Hudibras, 1664), paraphrasing this verse. The text's corporal-discipline has been a matter of ongoing interpretive-debate in Christian parenting-ethics.
'The righteous has enough to satisfy his appetite, but the belly of the wicked suffers want' tracks MT.
